findings.title: No-arg call isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but after this PR the only method with that name in the class hierarchy is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (declared in UsernamePasswordForm.java at line 160). There is no zero-argument overload in UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, so this is a compilation error ("no suitable method found for isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()") and the build fails. Either restore a no-arg `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` helper in UsernamePasswordForm (e.g. `return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled();`) or pass the user explicitly at this call site.

findings.title: user != null check in isConditionalPasskeysEnabled removes passkeys from the initial login page
findings.body: The new helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. Both call sites pass `context.getUser()`: `authenticate()` at line 115 and `challenge(context, error, field)` at line 137. On a normal first-time login the user is not yet identified, so `context.getUser()` is null and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never invoked. The rendered username/password page then lacks everything the passkeys conditional UI needs (the enableWebAuthnConditionalUI flag, the challenge/rpId attributes, the "username webauthn" autocomplete on the username field, and the webauth form). Previously fillContextForm ran in the user==null branch of authenticate(); the PR moved it out of that branch but gated it on the user being set, so it now runs ONLY during re-authentication — the condition was inverted instead of extended. This breaks ordinary passkey logins: the PR's own tests assert the webauthn form is present on the initial login page (e.g. PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey and passwordLoginWithExternalKey, PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey), so those tests would fail once the code compiles. The `&& user != null` condition should be dropped so the WebAuthn context is filled for both fresh logins and re-authentication.
